text: Account takeover of ACC-10011 via SIM swap. Customer Rachel Adams reported unauthorized wire transfer of $12,400 to unknown beneficiary. SIM swapped at carrier store using fake ID. Funds recovered via wire recall. Account re-secured with hardware token MFA.

Counterfeit check scheme targeting ACC-10027. Joseph Allen's business account received 4 counterfeit checks totaling $34,000 via mobile deposit. Checks drawn on non-existent accounts. Funds held per Reg CC exception hold. No loss to institution.

Elder financial exploitation. Margaret King (CUST-20028, age 82) had $45,000 withdrawn by newly added authorized signer (grandson). Unusual withdrawal pattern detected by teller. APS report filed. Funds partially recovered.

ATM skimming cluster at Shell station #4891, Denver CO. 12 compromised cards used for fraudulent ATM withdrawals totaling $14,400. Skimming device recovered by law enforcement. All affected customers reimbursed.

Payroll fraud at client company TechCorp Inc. Employee created 3 ghost employees in payroll system, diverting $67,500 over 6 months to accounts at our institution. Accounts frozen, funds partially recovered. Referred to FBI.

Romantic scam victim. Susan Clark (CUST-20016) wired $78,000 over 3 months to overseas accounts at direction of online romance scammer. Customer reported after family intervention. Recovery unlikely due to offshore beneficiaries.

Phishing-enabled ACH fraud on ACC-10029. Customer Brian Walker's credentials stolen via SMS phishing. Three unauthorized ACH debits totaling $4,200. Provisional credit issued within 10 days per Reg E. Mule accounts identified at other institutions.

Loan application fraud. Applicant submitted altered tax returns and fabricated pay stubs to obtain $250,000 commercial loan. Document verification detected inconsistencies. Application denied. Referred to FBI mortgage fraud unit.

First-party chargeback fraud. Customer filed 8 chargebacks totaling $6,200 for legitimate purchases. Merchant provided delivery confirmation and signed receipts for all transactions. Customer's chargeback privileges revoked.

Money mule network disruption. Five accounts (ACC-10050 through ACC-10054) identified as mule accounts receiving funds from BEC schemes. All accounts held by college students recruited via social media. Accounts closed, SARs filed.

Structuring investigation on ACC-10042 (Viktor Petrov / Petrov Trading LLC). Initial detection of sub-threshold cash deposits. 6 deposits totaling $55,000 over 3 days at different branches. SAR-2026-00147 filed. Investigation ongoing.

BEC wire fraud at Apex Manufacturing. Controller wired $187,500 based on spoofed CFO email. Wire recall initiated within 4 hours via SWIFT MT192. Partial recovery of $142,000. Enhanced wire authorization procedures implemented.

Synthetic identity fraud ring. ACC-10091 identified as part of 8-account synthetic identity ring across 4 institutions. SSNs belonging to minors combined with fabricated names. Total exposure $180,000. Joint investigation with FBI and other FIs via 314(b).

Check kiting investigation. Coastal Ventures LLC operating circular check scheme between ACC-10034 and ACC-10035. 14 checks totaling $156,000 exchanged in 10 days. Both accounts show negative collected balances. Administrative holds placed.

Card-not-present fraud on ACC-10023 (David Chen). 7 unauthorized online purchases totaling $3,847.50 within 48 hours. Card data compromised via unknown vector. Provisional credit issued. New card issued.

Expanded money laundering investigation on Petrov network. Graph analysis revealed 7 connected entities across 4 jurisdictions. Total fund flow of $284,750 traced through shell companies in Delaware, Cyprus, UAE, and Hong Kong.

Unauthorized Zelle transfer from ACC-10022. Catherine Hill reported $2,500 Zelle payment she did not authorize. Investigation found customer's email was compromised. Zelle does not guarantee recovery for authorized-appearing payments. Escalated to dispute.

Tax refund fraud. 12 tax refund direct deposits totaling $38,400 received into ACC-10050 within 2-week window. Refund amounts inconsistent with account holder's income. IRS notification sent. Funds held pending investigation.

Insider threat investigation. Teller employee (EMP-T0044) override patterns correlated with 5 fraud cases. Employee waived holds on 3 counterfeit check deposits and provided customer information to external parties. Terminated and referred to law enforcement.

Mobile deposit duplication. Customer deposited same $5,000 check via mobile at our institution and First National Bank simultaneously. Detected during clearing. Funds held. Customer claimed it was accidental. Account flagged.

Third-party payment processor abuse. Merchant account processed $340,000 in transactions for undisclosed sub-merchants selling counterfeit goods online. Merchant agreement terminated. Funds from pending settlements held.

Authorized push payment scam. Customer Carlos Rivera (ACC-10010) sent $8,500 via wire to scammer posing as IRS agent threatening arrest. Customer realized scam within 2 hours. Wire recall attempted but funds already withdrawn by beneficiary.

Dormant account activation fraud. ACC-10055 dormant for 3 years suddenly activated with $15,000 in deposits followed by $14,500 wire to overseas account. Account holder confirmed they did not reactivate. Credentials compromised via data breach.

Counterfeit card manufacturing ring. Law enforcement referral led to identification of 45 counterfeit cards linked to data breach at regional retailer. 8 cards used at our ATMs for $9,600 in withdrawals. ATM monitoring enhanced.

Invoice factoring fraud. Baker Auto Parts (ACC-10014) sold $120,000 in fabricated invoices to factoring company. Invoices referenced fictitious customers. Factoring company filed claim. Business account frozen pending resolution.

OFAC screening alert. Wire transfer from ACC-10042 to entity with 85% name match to SDN list entry. Meridian Holdings Ltd partially matches Meridian Capital (SDN-15542). Enhanced review required. Wire held pending OFAC determination.

Gift card laundering scheme. 200+ prepaid gift cards purchased using stolen credit card numbers at our merchant clients. Gift cards resold on secondary market. Total fraud loss $42,000 across 15 merchant locations.

Real estate money laundering. Customer used ACC-10039 (Steven Jackson, real estate agent) to facilitate all-cash purchase of $1.2M property through LLC. FinCEN GTO reporting triggered. Beneficial owner traced to foreign PEP.

Crypto-ATM structuring. Individual made 22 cash purchases at Bitcoin ATM located in our branch lobby, each under $3,000, totaling $62,000 over 2 weeks. ATM operator's KYC threshold set at $3,000. Referred to FinCEN.

Human trafficking financial indicators on ACC-10050. Multiple unrelated individuals making cash deposits. Address near known trafficking corridor. Cash withdrawals followed by prepaid card purchases. Referred to DHS and filed SAR with human trafficking narrative.

Corporate account compromise. ACC-10067 (Apex Manufacturing) online banking credentials stolen via spear-phishing. Attacker added new payee and initiated 2 ACH payments totaling $45,000 before detected. Both payments returned. No loss.

Ponzi scheme deposits. Investment company account received $890,000 in customer deposits over 4 months. Outflows primarily to principal's personal accounts and to early investors. SEC referral made after pattern analysis.

Deposit advance scheme. Customer made $8,000 check deposit, immediately requested $6,000 advance against uncollected funds (next-day availability per Reg CC). Check returned unpaid 3 days later. Loss of $6,000.

Correspondent banking abuse investigation. Foreign bank client processed $2.4M in wire transfers for customers in sanctioned jurisdiction through our correspondent account. Enhanced due diligence triggered. Correspondent relationship terminated.

Beneficial ownership concealment. Three LLCs (accounts ACC-10070, ACC-10071, ACC-10072) traced to same beneficial owner through nominee director network. Combined balance $450,000. CTA violation reported to FinCEN.

Peer-to-peer laundering network. 15 Venmo/Zelle accounts used to aggregate small payments ($50-$200 each) into consolidation account. Total throughput $34,000/month. Pattern consistent with narcotics proceeds laundering.

Loan stacking detected. Applicant obtained personal loans from 4 institutions totaling $120,000 within 30-day window using slightly varied name spellings. Total debt-to-income ratio exceeds 200%. Loans recalled where possible.

Merchant skimming at restaurant. POS terminal at Kim's BBQ (CUST-20008) found to have overlay skimmer. 34 customer cards compromised. Merchant cooperation in investigation. Equipment replaced and security training provided.

Forged document detection during KYC refresh. Customer CUST-20088 submitted passport (DOC-F9088) that failed automated verification. Font inconsistencies, metadata tampering, and template match to known fraud template. Account under enhanced review.

Pump and dump scheme. Customer traded $180,000 in penny stocks through brokerage account, coordinated with social media promotion on Reddit and Twitter. SEC referral triggered by unusual trading volume pattern.

Illegal online gambling transactions. Merchant account processed $560,000 in transactions coded as software consulting but traced to offshore gambling platform. Merchant terminated. Remaining settlement funds held.

FedNow exploitation attempt. Attacker used compromised credentials to initiate 8 FedNow instant payments totaling $12,000 within 3 minutes. Real-time fraud detection blocked 5 of 8 transactions. Loss limited to $4,500.

Trade-based money laundering. Import company over-invoiced electronic goods from China by 300%, moving $2.1M in excess value through trade finance instruments. Customs referral triggered investigation.

ACH return manipulation. Fraudster initiated 25 ACH debits against accounts at other institutions, harvesting $18,750 in provisional credits before returns were processed. Funds withdrawn via ATM before holds placed.

Marijuana banking compliance. State-licensed dispensary (ACC-10075) deposits $120,000/month in cash. All deposits filed as CTRs. Enhanced monitoring and quarterly review per FinCEN marijuana banking guidance.

Wire fraud via deepfake voice. Customer's CFO received phone call using AI-generated voice of CEO requesting emergency wire transfer of $225,000. Wire desk detected discrepancy in callback number. No funds lost. Reported to FBI IC3.

Document forgery ring. 8 accounts opened using professionally forged driver's licenses from 3 states. Ring identified through shared IP addresses during online account opening and common biometric anomalies.

Rapid fund movement on newly opened account ACC-10099 (Baltic Import Group). $47,000 deposited within first 2 weeks, immediately wired to accounts in Latvia and Lithuania. Account opened by Viktor Petrov (CUST-20015). Linked to CASE-2026-0011.

Cryptocurrency off-ramp investigation. ACC-10088 sent $59,500 to CryptoXchange Ltd (Estonia) over 10 days. Funds converted to Bitcoin and withdrawn to external wallet. Transaction trail broken at exchange. Linked to Petrov network.

Expanded Petrov network investigation consolidating CASE-2026-0011, CASE-2026-0026, CASE-2026-0048, and CASE-2026-0049. Total network exposure $284,750. Involves 7 entities across 4 jurisdictions. Joint investigation with FinCEN and FBI.
